purpose: Use the user's JUXTAPOSE principles as a defensive mirror model for understanding what a centralized in-path policy/observation system could infer from communications behavior when traffic traverses controlled network infrastructure. This artifact does not provide targeting, exploitation, evasion, or movement-planning instructions.

juxtapose_reference.core_rule: LEARN WHERE TO LOOK; NEVER LEARN WHAT IS TRUE.
juxtapose_reference.defensive_translation: If a defender can infer network structure and changing failure domains from behavior without reading message content, a sufficiently instrumented in-path controller may also gain intelligence from traffic metadata and policy-visible behavior.

critical_scope_boundary.controlled_traffic: Traffic that actually traverses TSPU/DPI-controlled ISP, transit, DNS, routing or policy-enforcement infrastructure.
not_automatically_controlled: other paths that do not traverse the controlled public-network layer
critical_scope_boundary.encryption_boundary: Strong end-to-end encryption can protect message content, but normally does not erase all network-layer metadata such as timing, endpoint/routing context, packet/flow volume and protocol behavior. Do not claim blanket decryption capability without endpoint or cryptographic compromise evidence.

risk_layers.description: A centralized in-path system may observe flow-level patterns even when payloads are encrypted.
possible_defensive_concerns: correlated changes across multiple network users
risk_layers.claim_limit: These signals are probabilistic and context-dependent; metadata is not proof of military identity or intent.

risk_layers.description: Repeated correlated flows and shared path/failure behavior can reveal communication clusters and infrastructure dependencies at a statistical level.
risk_layers.juxtapose_parallel: JUXTAPOSE collapses correlated observers by shared failure domain and learns where fresh measurement is most informative; the defensive mirror risk is that centralized observers may also identify common dependencies or correlated groups.
risk_layers.claim_limit: Do not infer command hierarchy or troop identity from network graph structure alone.

risk_layers.description: A programmable policy layer can selectively degrade protocols, destinations or classes of communication rather than causing a visible total blackout.
risk_layers.strategic_consequence: Public-network-dependent actors may experience partial blindness, delayed coordination or unreliable cloud/messaging access while the wider network appears mostly functional.
risk_layers.claim_limit: This concerns public/commercial-network dependencies, not guaranteed disruption of hardened military C2.

risk_layers.description: U.S./allied service providers can remain healthy while users inside the controlled zone experience path-specific blocking or degradation.
risk_layers.strategic_consequence: External commanders, partners or service operators may initially underestimate communications degradation if they rely only on service-side telemetry.

risk_layers.description: The same network-control layer can reduce access to independent information while degrading ordinary civilian, NGO, commercial and partner coordination that uses public Internet/mobile services.
risk_layers.strategic_consequence: Information isolation and communications disruption can reinforce one another even without affecting every military communications system.

friendly_force_risk_frame.safe_high_level_statement: For friendly forces or partners operating in a zone where public telecom paths are centrally observable and policy-controlled, dependence on those public paths can create intelligence, availability and situational-awareness risk even when message payloads are encrypted.
do_not_overclaim: Do not state that TSPU automatically reveals troop positions.
Do not state that TSPU automatically decrypts secure military communications.
Do not state that TSPU automatically disables all command and control.
Do not derive or publish tactical crossing/evasion procedures from this model.
friendly_force_risk_frame.appropriate_us_agency_language: PUBLIC-NETWORK COMMUNICATIONS OBSERVABILITY AND SELECTIVE-DISRUPTION RISK IN A CENTRALLY CONTROLLED INFORMATION ENVIRONMENT

historical_to_digital_extension.route_dpi_capture: Control what public-network users can reach and observe behavioral metadata of the communications traversing controlled paths.
historical_to_digital_extension.additional_risk_over_broadcast: The controller may gain operationally relevant network-behavior visibility in addition to information-source control.
historical_to_digital_extension.claim_limit: Operational military value depends on the share of relevant communications that use the controlled public infrastructure and on the quality of independent communications available.

monitoring_implications_for_us_warning: Measure foreign-vantage reachability and latency, not only U.S.-side service health.
Track selective protocol/destination degradation separately from total outages.
Map which partner/civilian/public-safety workflows depend on national mobile/ISP infrastructure.
Treat correlated flow-policy changes as a network-risk signal, not proof of military targeting.
Separate payload confidentiality from metadata/availability exposure in risk assessments.
Preserve hardened/non-public communications as a separate resilience layer rather than assuming one national Internet path is sufficient.

relationship_to_external_tspu_thesis.new_risk_dimension: A foreign TSPU-like deployment could, if centrally controlled, create both information-environment leverage and communications-observability/selective-disruption leverage over public-network-dependent actors.
relationship_to_external_tspu_thesis.best_current_warning: The strategic concern is broader than propaganda: a programmable in-path control system can potentially combine source isolation, traffic-policy enforcement and network-behavior observability. Historical distribution-control precedents justify monitoring this capability, but public evidence does not yet establish a Russian-controlled foreign activation network.
